title: What is the consulting career path, and what does up or out mean?
description: The levels from analyst to partner, typical time at each level, how titles differ at McKinsey, BCG and Bain, and what up-or-out really means.
hook: Consulting has one of the clearest career ladders of any profession, which is part of its appeal. It also has a reputation for "up or out", which can sound alarming. Here is how the path really works.
body:
The levels

  1. Analyst (entry level, usually from university). McKinsey calls this Business Analyst, BCG Associate and Bain Associate Consultant.
  2. Consultant or Associate (often the post-MBA entry point). You own a piece of the project.
  3. Manager (Engagement Manager or Project Leader). You run the team and the day-to-day project.
  4. Principal or Associate Partner. You oversee several projects and start selling work.
  5. Partner. You own client relationships and the firm's business.

How long it takes

Most levels last about two to three years. From entry-level analyst to partner typically takes around 8 to 12 years at MBB for strong performers. Big Four firms usually have more levels and a slower route to partner.

What up or out means

At many top firms, you are expected to be promoted within a certain window. If you are not progressing, you will usually be encouraged to leave, often with support finding your next role. In practice, many people leave by choice for other opportunities long before that point, and alumni networks are strong.

Entry points

  • From university: analyst roles.
  • From an MBA or advanced degree (PhD, law, medicine): consultant or associate roles.
  • Experienced hires: people with industry expertise can join at various levels, sometimes into specialist roles.
